Śreṇi : m. (pl.): Name of a people (?)

A. Description: Brought up in cowherds (gokule nityasaṁvṛddhāḥ) and highly skilled in fighting (yuddhe paramakovidāḥ)

.

B. Epic event: At night of the seventeenth day (niśi

), Saṁjaya, while reporting the death of Karṇa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, mentioned Śreṇis among those who were killed in thousands by Arjuna during the war (śreṇayo bahusāhasrāḥ saṁśaptakagaṇāś ca ye/te sarve pārtham āsādya gatā vaivasvatakṣayam//)

(perhaps, the word śreṇi does not refer to a people but means only ‘lines, rows of troops’ and refers to Gopālas who, though not directly mentioned are suggested by the expression (gokule nityasaṁvṛddhāḥ) and by their association with Saṁśaptakas, cf. Gopāla; see, however, the next entry).

Śreṇimant : m. (pl.): Name of a people (?)

Their glorious Kṣatriyas of noble birth, with weapons in hand, brought tribute in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (sujātayaḥ śreṇimantaḥ śreyāṁsaḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ/āhārṣuḥ kṣatriyā vittaṁ śataśo 'jātaśatrave//) 2. 48. 16 (for other details of the tribute see Śauṇḍika above). (Is Śreṇimant name of a people or an adjective of Kṣatriyas meaning ‘Kṣatriyas in troops’ ? See Sreṇi above).
